thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> service=redwood-canary-healthcheck, severity=critical. Canary pool us-west-2 showing 5xx >= 6% for last 3m. PD link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 auto-escalated to schedule `sre-oncall`. Notifying: @alyssa.

alyssa: ack PD12345. Looking at canary dashboard now. Which release is this?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout metadata: release=v3.4.7-canary, commit=8a3f2b1, batch=canary-3 (10% traffic). Healthchecks failing on model-serving pods behind route `embed-v3`.

ezra: thanks. seeing 502 spikes in the canary logs. throwing up `kvcache missing` in a few stacks. Snapshot of recent nginx proxy logs: 
```
2024-03-05T21:45:12Z node-3 embed_v3 502 0.12s "POST /v1/embeddings"
2024-03-05T21:45:14Z node-2 embed_v3 502 0.08s "POST /v1/embeddings"
2024-03-05T21:45:15Z node-3 runtime ERROR kvcache failed to fetch key, fallback miss=true
```

rachel: any upstream infra changes? autoscaler? kernel updates?

jordan: CI shows a new quant kernel landed in this release (PR #4123) that touches the kvcache fallback path. Might be related.

alyssa: ok. first priority: stop further canary traffic and roll back the canary to avoid customer impact. Plan: 1) scale canary to 0 traffic, 2) pin traffic back to stable, 3) revert release or rollback canary batch. Agree?

maria: +1. I'll reroute traffic. WFM to divert at edge for canary-3. Executing: `trafficctl set-fraction embed-v3 canary=0`.

deploy-bot: Command accepted: traffic fraction update in prog -> previous canary=0.10 now target=0.0. Routing changes deploying to edge nodes.

alyssa: acking as oncall. I'm going to mark incident severity P2 since we haven't seen customer reports but risk is non-zero. Updating PD.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 severity updated -> P2 by alyssa. Autopage throttling disabled for this incident.

ezra: while traffic drains, let's run quick test matrix against the older kernel to confirm kvcache behavior. Can we patch the quant kernel in a canary patch?

jordan: patching would take a while. prefer rollback of canary commit: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/embed-v3 --to-revision=8a3f2b0` (previous working revision). That should restore kvcache behavior.

alyssa: do it. maria, confirm that rolling back the canary is safe for the rest of the cluster (no DB migrations in this release).

maria: confirmed, no migrations. Initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback started: deployment/embed-v3 -> to revision 8a3f2b0. Progressing: 2/3 updated pods terminate, new pods pulling image.

rachel: monitoring p95/p99 and 5xx after rollback. also keeping watch on cost/latency dashboards.

incident-bot: PD12345 note added by alyssa: "Canary traffic diverted and canary release rolled back to previous revision. Monitoring for stabilization. No confirmed customer impact at time of update."

ezra: small telemetry blip at +2m, 5xx back to baseline ~0.3%. Nice.

jordan: logs from the new pods look normal. kvcache fetches returning hits again.

alyssa: good. I think we can start re-enabling traffic slowly once stable for 10m. Set slow ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 10% over 15m with abort conditions.

maria: started progressive ramp: steps=1,5,10; pause_on_failure=true; abort_if_5xx_gt=0.5%.

pagerduty-bot: PD12345: alerting suppressed during controlled ramp per oncall request.

rachel: I'll keep a watch on customer-facing SLOs and enable postmortem thread if anything reoccurs.

alyssa: handing off to rachel for stable-watch at 22:05 UTC. I'll remain available. Adding action items: (1) rollback revert PR (jordan) (2) test kernel patch in isolated env (ezra) (3) postmortem draft (rachel).

rachel: taking watch. noting timeline and participants. Creating incident channel notes and will open a postmortem draft after stabilization.

incident-bot: PD12345 resolved by alyssa -> status=closed at 2024-03-05T22:07:58Z. Resolution summary: canary rollback restored kvcache behavior; no confirmed customer impact; follow-ups assigned.

alyssa: nice job team, quick mitigation. Closing this thread and moving PM/action items to #postmortems. :thumbsup:
